title: Flat Tag Identity Concept
summary: define a tag as one assignable name while leaving interpretation and contextual nuance to linked document content
content_html:
Flat Tag Identity Concept

Purpose

Keep tag data limited to the identity needed to assign a tag to work and series records. Do not encode interpretative distinctions such as subject, domain, form, or theme as identity namespaces or conventional attributes.

Mental model

moss is the tag. A document may explain moss as depicted material, ecological domain, metaphor, theme, or any other useful context. Those readings are prose, not separate canonical tags and not analytical group membership.

flat tag identity
  -> assigned to work and series records
  -> linked one way to one explanatory document
  -> interpreted through document content

Invariants

  • tag_id is the globally unique normalized tag name.
  • The registry has neither group nor groups, and tag identity has no group prefix.
  • Group is not retained for filtering, scoring, coverage, styling, alias constraints, or report metadata.
  • Contextual differences between previously namespaced instances are resolved in one document rather than represented as parallel registry rows.
  • Assignment data records the tag only; it does not record which interpretation motivated an assignment.
  • The registry remains the assignment identity authority.
  • After Tag-document linking, the associated document is the semantic authority; registry prose is removed rather than synchronized.
  • The registry holds the one-way tag_id to doc_id relationship. Documents do not carry a tag_id back-reference, and unrelated documents may remain unreferenced.

Collision decision

Labels currently repeated across namespaces are not mechanically collapsed. Each is reviewed manually to choose one flat identity, its assignments and aliases, and document content that can carry the useful contextual distinctions.

The migration may preserve several genuinely different tags only by giving them genuinely different names. It must not recreate the removed group model through suffixes, hidden attributes, compatibility aliases, or report-only classification.
